body: We study self-modeling: an LLM's ability to answer questions about its own behavior. We focus on verifiable behavioral questions, such as whether a prompt edit would change the model's final answer. To measure this capability, we introduce a benchmark that tests diverse types of self-modeling questions. Current models show non-trivial but limited self-modeling skill, and make systematic mistakes on simple counterfactual questions about their own behavior. To improve self-modeling skill, we develop a scalable synthetic-data pipeline that produces self-modeling training data, and show that reinforcement-learning can improve aggregate self-modeling skill across three open-source model families with some transfer to held-out tasks. These gains, however, do not seem to constitute introspection consistently: improved self-modeling may not arise from privileged access to the model's internal decision process.
summaryZh: 本文系统研究了LLM的“自我建模”能力，即模型回答关于自身行为问题的能力。作者构建了一个包含多样化可验证行为问题的基准，发现当前模型在自我建模上存在局限性，尤其在反事实问题上表现不佳。通过开发合成数据流水线并结合强化学习，研究证明可以提升模型的自我建模能力，但指出这种提升可能并非源于模型对内部决策过程的真正内省。该工作为评估和改进大模型的自我认知能力提供了基准与方法论。
